LESSON: MAP READING AND INTERPRETATION

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Natural and Historic Built Environments
Topic 4.1: Map Reading and Interpretation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Map Reading and Interpretation
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: How can critical thinking be used in map interpretation?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. calculate areas of places on a topographical map
2. describe the different methods of representing physical features on topographical maps
3. apply critical thinking skills in map interpretation
4. value map reading and interpretation in day-to-day life

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Map Reading and Interpretation

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Map Reading and Interpretation

Teach
• Focus skill: calculate areas of places on a topographical map.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Map Reading and Interpretation.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Map Reading and Interpretation
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can critical thinking be used in map interpretation?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
